## Owner feedback — 2026-10-12

> One item for the future, just to keep track of in our issues, is that the RetroAchievements Pocket Nova had my RetroAchievements info already on it. If I had done that, or we agreed to do that in an earlier step, that's fine. I just wanted to make sure we're not accidentally giving every handheld my RetroAchievements username and password.

Already written: D-INFRA-006/007 distinguish personal engineering images from public firmware; #68 covers device-entered RetroAchievements access. #557 accepted Nova's update with complete parsed settings/credential preservation. That proves the update preserved prior state, not who first entered the sign-in, and does not alone prove clean image defaults.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: inspect exact firmware/defaults and clean/retained-storage guest behavior with synthetic accounts. Retained private deployment hashes may establish unchanged owner state without new device access. No credential values, values-derived hashes, personal names, or tokens belong in this issue or public evidence.

- [ ] Record a source/artifact-bound, value-free inventory separating player username/password/token, developer API identity, and previously retained device settings.
- [x] Trace existing Nova sign-in to earlier evidence or explicitly retain unknown origin; never infer a clean image from a successful state-preserving upgrade.
- [ ] Verify a clean image starts with no personal player account and retained-storage upgrades keep the selected user's account, using disposable VM evidence and unchanged-settings receipts.
- [ ] Verify public release preflight refuses personal build/runtime credentials; synthetic positive/negative fixtures exercise the guard and final accepted payload is checked. Repair any confirmed leak before publication.

Future assurance task linked to #528/#344; initial read-only artifact triage may run now. No confirmed credential leak, no device mutation, and no public release permission inferred.
## Initial read-only triage

Initial triage of accepted Nova bc9dfe8141 SYSTEM: exact payload SHA matches accepted firmware. Shipped system.cfg has empty RetroAchievements username/password; shipped RetroArch has empty username/password/token; no populated matching account fields were found in shipped ES settings or etc/retroarch.cfg. EmulationStation's known compiled ScreenScraper and RetroAchievements developer URL-pair patterns are absent. Existing private #557 receipts prove all parsed settings unchanged through the update. This supports retained device state, not an image-seeded account; original sign-in author remains unknown. No device access, credential display, or claim of a universal whole-image secret scan. The temporary SYSTEM extraction was removed. The value-free receipt is committed in 960b4d8c358b1e74b501ffdc329532be67cf7f6e; see the evidence link below after record publication.

Current tools/fork-publish-release is a prepare-only planner and explicitly leaves artifact credential inspection as a gate; historical docs describing its old uploader/embedded-key rejection are not proof of a current executable publication check. Verify that gate in this task before public distribution.

Evidence record: [owner-feedback triage](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/960b4d8c358b1e74b501ffdc329532be67cf7f6e/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-12-owner-feedback/README.md).

## Active work — October 12

Owner: “Let's work through 565, 566, and 567 now.” Moved into M7.P5 in that order. #569 read-only incident diagnosis is an immediate interruption; #564 and #493 remain the next foundation/build gates. Existing acceptance criteria and VM-first scope remain.

## Activity-history isolation and Nova provenance — October 13

Owner, verbatim:
> There definitely is metadata that's gotten onto the Retroid Pocket Nova. As I mentioned before, for example, it shows that backup saves to the cloud ran on 9/30/2026, and that restore saves from the cloud also ran on 9/30/2026. But there haven't been any ROMs on this console until now, so somehow we've put config settings and system metadata on here that didn't originate on this device. It's a little concerning if that's somehow part of our installation process, because it means we've muddled the device history, and we definitely don't want this happening on a fresh install.

Also includes the owner's Mario Tennis/Sonic Recently Played report in issuecomment-6137928961. This broadens the existing release-isolation gate beyond credentials: clean installs must not inherit another installation's activity, QA fixture state, or game history. Updates must preserve legitimate existing state.

Source/history triage: accepted ES c8dc72cf9e includes a game in Recently Played when PlayCount compares greater than "0"; the collection does not prove a launch on this particular device. The September 29 work log records the first Nova fork installation as an update over stock ROCKNIX, and September 30 records Dropbox setup and restore-flow troubleshooting on the Nova. Those records are leads, not proof of the provenance or success of either displayed operation. Do not assert contamination or dismiss it without reading the relevant stamp/metadata bytes.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes for clean-image isolation, stamp semantics, metadata loading and retained-storage upgrade behavior using synthetic data. Historical attribution first uses preserved records and scoped read-only Nova metadata. No cloud requests, games, restores, config changes or history deletion are authorized by this investigation.

Acceptance criteria, additional to the account criteria above:
- [x] Bind displayed backup/restore dates to their actual local stamp fields and status; distinguish attempted, completed-empty and data-transferring operations using retained logs where available.
- [x] Trace the two Recent entries to metadata fields and available setup/copy/restore records; state any remaining unknown origin explicitly.
- [ ] Inspect exact firmware/default payloads and clean-boot storage for cloud activity stamps, play-history metadata, connection state and QA residue; publish only value-free results.
- [ ] Exercise the isolation gate with synthetic contaminated and clean payloads; fresh installation has no fabricated activity while upgrade preserves legitimate existing history.

No confirmed image contamination yet. Existing credential-only triage does not satisfy the expanded history checks.


## Manual library copy and operational-script scope — October 13

Owner, verbatim:

> With the Pocket Nova, we're not entirely sure. I was specifically curious if any of our post-transfer scripts, cleanup scripts, or anything else might have put data on them. I guess there's not an easy way to figure out historically if we transferred some personal settings accidentally at some point. Having the controls in place to ensure a clean install in the future may be the best we can do for now, and there isn't really enough information to do real forensic analysis.
> 
> My bigger concern is also just if this could happen accidentally to someone. One question is: if someone's doing transfers from a computer to a microSD card of directories, is there information in the directories, potentially? I copied just ROM directories, but I'm curious if that could have had additional information. Also, if there's anything we'd gain from me powering on the handheld and you connecting, we can experiment with that as well.

Transfer clarification, verbatim:

> I used the USB gadget function to connect the Nova to my computer and then transferred the files by hand from the ROMs directory that's in the Dropbox to the microSD card directory.

The installed-source contract already allows library metadata to travel: D-CLOUD-049 places game lists in game content. Accepted distribution bc9dfe8141 exposes /storage/roms through the USB MTP Roms share. Accepted ES c8dc72cf9e prefers a system-folder gamelist.xml over its internal fallback, loads playcount/lastplayed/favorite/gametime, and uses positive playcount for Recently Played. Copying a whole Dropbox library folder can therefore import history without any cloud sign-in on the recipient. This is a supported mechanism and a leading explanation, not a verified reconstruction of this copy. No source/destination file comparison has been performed.

Normal account configuration and cloud activity stamps live outside that exported ROM tree. The reviewed October9 Nova preparation wrapper disables startup/game-exit sync using the Nova's existing local settings and archives those local originals; unrelated state is checked against its pre-action binding. It does not import another device's configuration. First-boot/post-update scripts do copy defaults from the firmware into storage, so clean final-payload checks remain necessary. This review does not exclude all earlier unrecorded operations.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: synthetic folder-copy/import behavior and the separation from accounts/activity stamps belong in disposable VM fixtures. Existing local source/records suffice for the current explanation; no physical-device operation is required. A later optional read-only comparison of the active Nova game list against the original computer/Dropbox copy could strengthen provenance but would not identify the original credential writer. No experiment, launch, cloud request, cleanup or configuration mutation is authorized by this note.

- [x] Record source-bound metadata paths and operational-script scope, distinguishing imported library history from firmware-seeded or retained account state. Evidence: accepted source paths above and docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-nova-library-copy.md.
- [x] Include a synthetic library-copy case in #565 VM qualification: ROM-only versus ROM-plus-gamelist.xml, expected Recent behavior, and unchanged account/activity-stamp state. Retain source-bound fixture results.


## October13 baseline results — completed within scope

The three provenance criteria above are satisfied by the published memory-state-followup/nova-provenance.md, nova-library-copy.md and nova-readonly-followup.md records: retain unknown original account writer, bind September30 empty restore/0B backup, and identify ROM-side play history without claiming historical copy attribution.

The synthetic library-copy criterion now passes: identical stub ROM bytes alone yield0 plays/no Recent entry; adding gamelist.xml yields5 plays/imported date/Recent membership, with selected account and cloud activity fields unchanged. No game or cloud operation. Recent was explicitly enabled; this surfaced inherited default bug #578. Original404-masking and restart-limit failures remain recorded separately; third library owner passes0. [Exact source, fixture results and limitations](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/4d5c26807d92e0535b8a5e796c8e6446aab47c6c/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-library-wifi-baseline/README.md).

Final candidate payload, clean first boot and actual retained-storage upgrade remain open. No universal image-cleanliness or original Nova account attribution claim. VM stopped; disk/UEFI/access material retired,2247536640allocated bytes released.

comments.body: Clean VM evidence now covers seven known default/runtime account configuration files, with zero populated player/developer credential fields. This used fresh VM20 storage and no entered account; it is not a whole-image secret scan or retained-account upgrade. Evidence: docs/qa-logs/2026-10-12-cloud-configuration/clean-vm-accounts.json. The executable public release credential gate and retained-account upgrade proof remain open; no source implementation is claimed.

## Additional Nova state-provenance question

Owner, verbatim:
> Unrelated to this, but when I first loaded roms onto the Retroid Pocket Nova, it had two games in the recently played gamelist already. Could this be something we can explain? I'm trying to think how that playlist could have been populated if there's no cloud sync happening. I'm not sure if this was config we populated when putting on the OS, or if something else transferred it. It had Mario Tennis and Sonic already on it, and I'm just trying to think of why.

This extends the existing provenance investigation while #570 browser controls remain active. Inspect preserved deployment/setup records and actual ES recent-list predicates; distinguish preexisting storage, gamelist metadata copied with a library/backup, QA seeding and an actual local launch. Do not infer cloud sync or a local launch merely from a collection entry. Any read-only device inspection is limited to relevant noncredential metadata; no gameplay, sync, restore or history edits.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes for proving how recent entries are derived from synthetic metadata. The owner's historical provenance first needs existing exact records/read-only metadata; no VM can recreate absent historical evidence.

- [ ] Cite current recent-collection predicate and the fields that produce membership.
- [ ] Compare Nova preparation/preservation history and relevant metadata; name what is established and what cannot be attributed.
- [ ] If image/fixture contamination is found, reproduce synthetically and include it in the artifact-isolation gate before publication.

Read-only follow-up ties the reported September30 dates to retained operation evidence: restore stamp1790811786 is2026-09-30T23:43:06Z; backup stamp1790811792 is23:43:12Z. Both code0. The preserved Nova log shows restore treated the absent legacy saves root as empty; backup said nothing to transfer and0B/0B. Thus these dates are consistent with operations on an empty library, not by themselves evidence that another device's activity stamps were installed. Current read-only stamp readback matches the earlier evidence exactly.

The two Recent entries are now bound to local gamelist metadata: playcount5/lastplayed20260908T031024 and playcount1/lastplayed20260906T014729. Both precede the Nova's first fork update. Accepted ES CollectionSystemManager.cpp:1043 selects Recent membership from PlayCount > "0". The gamelist files currently have October12 modification times; that alone does not identify copying, restore, scraper or writeback. The exact arrival path remains unknown. No history or account fields were edited, no games started and no provider request made.

Source and artifact isolation remains open: credential-only default checks do not establish clean play-history/activity defaults. This is a provenance refinement, not closure of #565.

Owner continuation, verbatim:
> Let's continue the investigations around the different items in M7 to see what we can do to further isolate anything that might give us savings in terms of memory pressure. The rclone backend experience improves. I also want to make sure we address the various issues that came up with my RetroAchievements Pocket Nova testing around the starting state of that device and ensuring we have an understanding of why various metadata seem to already be present.

Current execution: #570 existing trace CPU/reclaim attribution and a parallel exact-WebKit memory-policy source candidate; #565 Nova provenance plus an executable clean-image/activity gate. Main runtime remains serialized; no owner account/device mutations or discarded offline functions. Can this be done on the VM? Yes for browser controls and clean/retained state gates. Existing historical provenance uses preserved records; a VM cannot invent absent history. Prior diagnostic delivery1a37cde40a is complete with both hosted checks and all original exits0; do not replay retired owners.

Visible owners: pix-memory w4:p8 in feature/m7-browser-memory-570 prepares only docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-browser-memory-policy/; pix-nova w4:p9 in feature/m7-clean-state-565 prepares scoped gate/test/tool integration plus docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-clean-state-565/. Both source-only. Coordinator w4:p2 owns runtime, shared records and integration; a reused internal read-only investigator traces Nova history. No full build/cache copy is allocated. Analysis of retained browser traces is new arithmetic over prior runtime, not a new VM trial. Source candidates/fixtures return immutable for review before serialized tests.

# #565 clean-state source candidate runtime allocation

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. After the #570 matrix and its exact guest are consumed/retired, boot a separate fresh VM20 from the verified accepted image:2048MiB,640x480,16GiB disk,loopbackSSH10577/VNC62,owned pidfile/serial/OVMF. No owner device/provider/config data. Use candidate63e05cd728acd1d2a76dffc1c4b1d7fd75fa3fab, whose source corrections received independent review. No integration/promotion yet.

First run its value-free --root / --mode first-boot --require-ready through serial before staging QA fixture files or any account/history. Require actual guest exit plus readiness witness; a refusal is retained and is not proof of contamination until classified against actual source/defaults. Then provision only a fresh synthetic QA SSH key and stage the gate/test pair under guest /tmp, run bounded --self-test controls in a watched owner, collect value-free output and exact exits. These controls exercise synthetic roots including contaminated defaults, retained allowances, malformed inputs and the reviewed fixes; they do not simulate a real OS upgrade by themselves. No final-payload reader test or publication is authorized by this small allocation; mcopy availability must be resolved separately before payload qualification.

No browser, provider, real account, gameplay or cloud operation. Bound fixture child to120s; serial proof180s. Record source/guest identities, actual results and input hashes; retire exact disk/OVMF/keys when done. Source and first-boot failures go back to pix-nova for correction, not bypasses. No full build/cache copy.

### #565 next bounded final-payload reader controls

Can this be done on the VM? The first-boot and synthetic-root policy have been
executed in the disposable OS VM. The additional component under test is the
host release-preparation program and its host filesystem readers; the OS guest
does not ship mcopy, mksquashfs, unsquashfs, sfdisk or debugfs. Execute this host
entrypoint as the normal unprivileged build user against synthetic regular
files in a fresh bounded owner, with no mounts, image build, network request,
owner data or release publication. This is host-tool qualification, not a
substitute for the guest's first-boot/upgrade checks.

After the active first-boot VM is consumed and retired, freeze the corrected
pix-nova commit plus its release helper and dependencies in a new owner. Use
the installed filesystem utilities plus the existing read-only accepted
toolchain mcopy4.0.49 (verified executable; no installation or cache mutation).
Run --payload-tests once with a180second outer bound and1GiB scratch budget.
It creates tiny synthetic SquashFS, update tar, FAT/ext4 install-image files
and release bundles; clean inputs must pass, populated credentials/history,
storage seeds, literal bracketed filenames and malformed/missing readers must
refuse without values in output. Prepared release JSON is not publishing.
Retain actual fixture/launcher/wrapper/watcher exits and byte identities, delete
temporary payloads after the run, and return any failure for source correction.
No real final firmware artifact is asserted clean by these synthetic controls.

Selected clean-state gate and Nova provenance findings are now published in `e398cbb9977e29173616a067c0e26b09e09e7ba2`.

**Nova history:** its first fork installation on September 29 was an in-place update preserving storage. The recorded deployment chain contains no config/gamelist copy, but cannot exclude UI or unrecorded actions. The effective on-disk account combination was incomplete that day; populated fields existed before the October 9 update. Their original author/entry path remains unknown. September 30 records show an empty restore followed by a 0 B backup, with settings backup skipped. Those stamps do not prove transferred ROMs/settings. The two Recent entries have positive playcounts and dates predating the first fork install; metadata explains list membership, not gameplay on this Nova. [Value-free provenance and limitations](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/e398cbb9977e29173616a067c0e26b09e09e7ba2/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-memory-state-followup/nova-provenance.md).

**Executable protection:** `tools/pixelelated-state-check` checks selected account/cloud/activity/history/QA surfaces, refuses required unreadable/malformed inputs, and is integrated into the prepare-only release helper. It is not a universal whole-image secret scanner and does not publish releases.

- Actual ready fresh VM20 selected-state check: PASS, exit 0.
- Expanded guest synthetic-root controls: 113 PASS, exit 0.
- Final host root/payload/release-preparation controls: 142 PASS, exit 0, 10.22 seconds, 188,178,432 bytes peak scratch, removed afterward.

Real-runtime coverage found and corrected comment-only shipped RetroArch defaults, legitimate zero-work startup scrub state, retained partial/reordered scrub records, and canonical unused ext4 directory slots. Original failures and diagnostic runs remain failures. Final gate bytes differ from the guest-tested revision only in the `empty_ext4` AST function; the first-boot path is unchanged. This is composed source-bound qualification, not a second guest run of the final file.

[Source bindings, original failures, passing controls and retirement](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/e398cbb9977e29173616a067c0e26b09e09e7ba2/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-clean-state-runtime/README.md). The fresh VM/disk/UEFI were retired, recovering 2,244,313,088 allocated bytes. No owner state was changed or reset.

Still required: inspect the actual next candidate payload, verify its clean first boot, and run a real retained-storage upgrade with synthetic account/history preservation. The component controls do not replace that upgrade. #565 remains open; the original provenance uncertainty remains explicit.

Owner authorization, October 13:
> I just brought the Pocket Nova online, and you have my approval to do any read-only research on the device necessary as we do troubleshooting for this issue.

Read-only plan: identify the active ROM/fallback/recovery game-list sources for the two reported games, inspect timestamps and safe metadata fields, and inspect retained local deployment archives/receipt presence and selected account-field equality without disclosing values or value-derived hashes. Read known startup/script identities and bounded selected log categories if useful. Use stdin collectors, no staged device files, no provider/cloud requests, no emulator/menu/input/reboot or settings changes.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes for behavior: the synthetic library-copy fixture remains a VM task. This read is historical artifact acquisition from the owner's actual Nova, not a software qualification experiment or evidence that the VM is insufficient for behavior testing. Existing private records and current on-device artifacts may narrow provenance; they cannot recreate missing history or establish the original writer from timestamps alone.

Approved read-only Nova follow-up is complete; plan/authorization is issuecomment-6147924942.

The two reported histories are in game lists beside the GBA and Genesis ROMs. Corresponding ROMs exist and references are relative. Neither system has a fallback game list or recovery directory in the inspected ES locations; the legacy ES path resolves to the current config directory. Under the accepted loading rules, the in-folder lists supply this metadata. Their October12 modification times do not establish the initial copy time; no useful birth time was returned. The original computer/Dropbox files have not been compared, so the reported manual USB copy remains a supported, strong explanation rather than a proven transfer reconstruction.

The Nova retains the October9 preparation archive. Its original system.cfg matches the original private plan binding. All four selected current global RetroAchievements account fields are nonempty and exactly match that pre-preparation original. These fields therefore existed before that preparation step. The accepted receipt's19 protected file records match before/after, and all three preserved preparation scripts match both their plan hashes and retained host source. The wrapper edits the two local automatic-sync flags and archives local originals; no foreign configuration import was found in that wrapper. Original account entry before October9 remains unknown.

The September30 empty-operation stamps remain unchanged. No custom autostart or ES script-hook path was present in the two inspected locations. These are bounded observations, not a whole-device forensic guarantee.

One collector initially omitted the global. prefix from account identifiers; its account-only absence outputs are explicitly invalidated. A corrected separate read using verified identifiers supplies all account findings above. No credential values or value-derived hashes are published. Original private evidence and correction are preserved.

All three bounded stdin-only collectors returned0 and exited. No device file was staged, no setting/game/input/reboot operation occurred, and no provider request was made. Normal SSH access logs may still be written by the device. Source trace and sanitized readback notes are locally committed on feature/m7-player-setup as4b1c7794b2 and ef8e961ad8, pending normal record delivery. The pending synthetic library-copy VM case and next firmware clean/retained qualification remain unchanged; no further owner-device experiment is needed for this explanation.

Afternoon records delivered on `next` at `71b932ab3235ac252ef37cb8391e08807a76de91`: `4b1c7794b2` ROM-folder import source trace and `ef8e961ad8` approved read-only provenance follow-up are now published. Both exact-head record/wordlist CI checks passed; original delivery channels are0 and actual processes exited. No new runtime proof or device action is implied. The actual future payload, clean/retained-upgrade and synthetic library-copy criteria remain open.

## Testing-first continuation — October 13

Owner:
> Got it. Can we start working through all of these issues we've discovered and figure out what we need to do to be able to start bringing them to resolution? There's additional testing to do. Let's go ahead and do that first. I'd like to be able to work towards our next release candidate.

Can this be done on the VM? **Yes.** Start a fresh disposable accepted VM20 guest, 8GiB RAM/4vCPU/16GiB sparse disk/640x480, to qualify the synthetic ROM-only versus ROM+gamelist import case (#565) and reproduce initial/delayed/refreshed/empty/error Wi-Fi layout (#577). No owner's saves, account, cloud or handheld is used. Existing accepted image/source and exact VM profile/commands are recorded. Keep unchanged-image reproduction separate from next-candidate qualification.

Current allocation: /workspace/tmp/pix-m7-baseline-tests-20261013, at most8GiB host scratch,8GiB guest RAM, ports10580/5974 checked free. Host has over2.8TB free and50GiB available memory; existing swap occupancy is recorded without changing host swap. Durable watch-build/watch-job owners plus active result consumption supervise each stage; no disconnected alert is claimed. Stop the exact VM and retire its disk/UEFI/access material after compact evidence is accepted.

#570 remains the first product fix to qualify, but #493's final criterion explicitly requires capacity/retention enforcement **before compilation**, including the actual ES candidate. No compiler or full cache copy starts in this baseline stage. Put #493 at that dependency boundary, while the existing-image tests proceed. Diagnostic allocator interposition is already complete and will not be repeated as a substitute for compiling the actual change.
